- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.4) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for downward risk.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a 2–5 day “cool-down” lag, reducing forecast by 1–2% per day post-spike.
- If 3+ consecutive forecast days are above true outcome, apply mean reversion: subtract 0.5–1.5% from next 3–5 days’ forecast.
- If sentiment history shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive +0.6+), model often fails to cap peak; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent high.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3 days, model often lags; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% per day for next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate in early forecast days (1–7) when sentiment is rising; reduce first 3–5 forecast values by 1–2%.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days below 70), model often ignores it; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
